title: Minimum Splits of Powers of Two to Form Target
description: You are given an array `nums` in which every element is a non-negative integer power of two (`2^k` for `0 <= k <= 30`), and a positive integer `target`. In one operation, you may choose an element `nums[i] > 1`, remove it from `nums`, and append two copies of `nums[i] / 2`. Return the minimum number of operations needed so that some subsequence of `nums` sums to `target`, or `-1` if it is impossible.
constraints: 1 <= nums[i] <= 2^30 and nums[i] is a power of two.
hints: A solution exists if and only if the total sum of `nums` is at least `target`. Count how many copies `cnt[b]` of each power `2^b` you hold.

Process bits `b = 0..30` greedily: if bit `b` of `target` is `1` and `cnt[b] == 0`, borrow the smallest available `j > b` with `cnt[j] > 0` (costing `j - b` splits and populating one copy at each bit `b..j - 1`), then carry `cnt[b] // 2` pairs up to `cnt[b + 1]`.

examples.explanation: Split 8 into 4 + 4 (1 operation) so subsequence [1, 2, 4] sums to 7.
Combine 1+1+2 = 4, and split 32 -> 16+16 -> 8+8 (2 operations) to reach 4 + 8 = 12.
The total sum of [1, 32, 1] is 34 < 35, so target 35 is unreachable.
